clue.text: Belgrade soccer club first to transfer winger

parts.note: Red Star Belgrade is the famous football club of the Serbian capital

indicators.note: first, with 'to' as link, asks for the opening letter of the word transfer

explanation.surface: A Serbian football club is about to sign a new wide player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winger' looks like a footballer on the wing, but here it means a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird is a winged creature, and the redstart is a small songbird with a reddish tail.

clue.text: Rumours of sightings all started right here

definitions.text: Rumours of sightings all started right here

parts.words: Rumours of sightings all started right here
parts.note: points to the New Mexico town where tales of a crashed UFO and alien visitors began in 1947

explanation.surface: Identifying the birthplace of UFO rumours.
explanation.definitionFit: This town in New Mexico is the famous origin of the 1947 flying saucer crash story.

clue.text: Where yellow, brown and green balls start in a row

parts.words: Where yellow, brown and green balls start
parts.note: in snooker these three balls are placed on the D, a semicircle at the baulk end
taken as written

explanation.surface: Describing snooker balls set out in a line.
explanation.walkthrough: In snooker, the D is the semicircle marked on the table where those three coloured balls are spotted.
explanation.definitionFit: A din is a loud noise, which is what a row means in British speech.

clue.text: Collectively, authors have failed test about West Bank city

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the anagram goes round the city
failed means broken down, so these letters are put in a new order

parts.note: Hebron is a Palestinian city in the West Bank

explanation.surface: Writers have failed an exam about a Palestinian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failed' reads as the authors failing, but it scrambles the word test, and 'about' wraps those letters round the Palestinian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlotte, Emily and Anne were three writing sisters, so together they form a group of authors.

clue.text: Wild boar's head in sack

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the letter goes within the other word

parts.note: to sack a town is to plunder it, to raid it

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A boar's head stuffed into a bag.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabid animal is mad and frenzied, so it is wild in behaviour.

clue.text: Radii drawn in sort of black pen

indicators.note: drawn in means pulled inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: coal-black is a shade of black, so coal is a sort of black
R is the abbreviation for radius, so two of them make RR

explanation.surface: A geometry instruction about drawing radii with a particular kind of black pen.
explanation.definitionFit: An enclosure for livestock is a pen, the same thing as a ranch enclosure.

clue.text: Warning from engineering section

indicators.note: a section is a part cut out of something, so the answer lies within these words

explanation.surface: A caution issued by an engineering department.
explanation.definitionFit: A portent is a sign of what is to come, often a warning of trouble.

clue.text: Grip lost in long hair — odd

indicators.note: lost means astray, so the letters wander into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone loses their hold, oddly, in long hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' rearranges LONG HAIR and ODD together.
explanation.definitionFit: A car's ability to keep traction on the road is its grip.

clue.text: US city and what it owes outspoken, badly behaved girl

parts.note: LA, Los Angeles, is a US city

indicators.note: spoken out loud, so a word is replaced by one that sounds the same

parts.note: what a city owes is its debt

explanation.surface: Los Angeles and its debts personified as a rowdy young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: DEBT, with its silent B, sounds like DETTE.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a young woman who behaves boisterously, drinking and carousing like a lad.

clue.text: Almost grasp 27s election campaign

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter of the word for grasp goes

parts.note: a hug is a tight grasp
the answer to 27 across means a swindle, and swindles are also called stings

explanation.surface: Barely grasping some swindles in an election campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference points to 27 across; its answer, plural, gives STINGS.
explanation.definitionFit: Speeches and canvassing before a British election are called the hustings, the campaign trail.

clue.text: Delightful time with road movie?

parts.note: read as de-light-ful, the time when the light goes away: the end of the day
a boulevard is a broad city road

explanation.surface: A happy moment combined with a road film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delightful' must be split as de-light: the time of losing daylight.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of Billy Wilder's 1950 Hollywood film starring Gloria Swanson, hence the question mark example.

clue.text: Charge traffic cops on departure

parts.note: reads like police on traffic duty charging someone leaving, but means a levy imposed on goods traded out of the country

explanation.surface: Traffic police arrest someone as they leave.
explanation.definitionFit: A tax on goods leaving a country is a charge levied on outgoing trade at the point of departure.

clue.text: Check on people with little in common

definitions.text: Check on people with little in common

parts.words: Check on people with little in common
parts.note: reads as people with nothing shared, but means a snare holding back those with little money

explanation.surface: Investigating a group with nothing to share.
explanation.definitionFit: A situation where low earners are kept poor, because more income loses them benefits, is a check on them.

clue.text: Injection of crack

definitions.meaning: a jab of a drug from a needle
an attempt, as in have a go

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are everyday meanings of the word: a jab with a needle, and a try at something.

clue.text: Old Russian city street and a girl struggling to follow it

indicators.note: to follow it means coming after the street
struggling means flailing, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A girl struggles along a road in an old Soviet city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggling' rearranges AND A GIRL into ALINGRAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Volgograd was formerly named after Stalin, so it is an old Russian city name.

clue.text: Joke, malicious, about what stimulant will do

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the whole run of letters reads backwards

parts.note: a pun is a joke built on wordplay
evil means wicked or malicious

explanation.surface: A nasty joke about the effect of a drug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns the whole run backwards: PUNEVIL reversed becomes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A stimulant enlivens, so it will make someone more lively and energetic.

clue.text: Surveys about a way to get trees cut back

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the surveys go round the other letters

parts.note: polls are surveys of opinion
Rd is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: Opinion polls about how to get trees pruned.
explanation.definitionFit: Trees with their branches cut back to the trunk to encourage dense new growth are so called.

clue.text: Corruption of a Latin and English female name

indicators.note: corruption means a debased or altered form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A girl's name said to come from a debased mix of Latin and English.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the name's etymology; 'Corruption of' rearranges the A and Latin before English is added.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a girl's given name, so it is an example of a female name.

clue.text: Almost perfect chamber music composer

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter of the word for perfect is dropped

parts.note: pure means flawless or perfect
a cell is a small chamber, as in a prison

explanation.surface: Praising a composer of chamber music as nearly flawless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chamber music' reads as one phrase, but chamber is CELL and music belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Purcell was the great English Baroque composer of the seventeenth century.

clue.text: China has to maintain tedious bureaucracy

parts.note: in cockney rhyming slang china plate means mate, a pal
to aver is to maintain or assert

explanation.surface: China must uphold its tiresome red tape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country, but is rhyming slang: china plate means mate.
explanation.definitionFit: Fuss and long-winded procedure is called this, much like tiresome red tape.

clue.text: Only one playing thus is in a group

parts.note: so means in this way, thus

indicators.note: the word is placed in, so it goes inside the group

parts.note: a lot is a group or batch of things
taken as written

explanation.surface: A musician performing alone within an ensemble.
explanation.definitionFit: A solo performer is the single musician playing while the rest are silent.

clue.text: Rubbish I want to be on about can matter?

indicators.note: in a down clue to be on means placed on top of the next piece
rubbish means worthless mess, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A grumble about what a tin can is made of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rubbish' reads as junk but is the anagram signal for I want; in a down clue, 'to be on' places it above the word for about.
explanation.definitionFit: Articles made of tin, like cans, are the stuff a can is made from, its matter.

clue.text: Songs don't work on the radio

indicators.note: heard on the radio, so a word is replaced by one that sounds the same

parts.note: to laze is to idle and not work

explanation.surface: A complaint that some songs fail when broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: A lay is an old word for a ballad or short song, so the plural means songs.

clue.text: Minute change in uranium compound that dispatches many slugs

indicators.note: compound means mixed together, so these letters are combined in a new order

parts.note: U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: A chemistry note about altering a uranium compound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compound' looks like a chemical noun but is the anagram signal; 'slugs' are bullets, not garden pests.
explanation.definitionFit: Slugs is slang for bullets, and an automatic weapon fires many in rapid succession.

clue.text: Villain tips off the boys in blue

indicators.note: tips off means the leading letters are cut from each word

parts.note: the navy, whose sailors wear blue

explanation.surface: A criminal informs the police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tips off' looks like informing, but means dropping the first letters of THE and NAVY.
explanation.definitionFit: In films a heavy is the menacing bad guy, the villain's role.

clue.text: Homeless child with a condition

parts.note: if introduces a condition

explanation.surface: A street child with a precondition.
explanation.definitionFit: A stray, abandoned child is called this, especially a thin neglected one.

clue.text: Runs out of gas?

parts.note: runs is slang for a loose bowel, and gas is idle talk: a looseness of chatter that never stops

explanation.surface: A car stopping because its fuel tank is empty.
explanation.definitionFit: A humorous idiom for an uncontrollable flow of talk, likened to a bowel complaint.

clue.text: Snowshoes are completely pointless and that surprises me!

indicators.note: points are the compass directions N, S, E and W, and every one is removed from the word

explanation.surface: Snowshoes are useless, and that is a surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing every compass point from SNOWSHOES leaves just O, H and O.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of surprise, used when something unexpected is noticed.

clue.text: Do dead letters get cancelled?

parts.note: RIP, rest in peace, are the letters written for the dead
an event called off is off, cancelled

explanation.surface: Asking whether undeliverable post gets cancelled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dead letters' suggests undeliverable mail; here it is the inscription RIP.
explanation.definitionFit: To do someone is slang for swindling them, which is cheating them out of money.

clue.text: Signs of disorder as empty secondary modern is trashed

indicators.note: empty means the inside is removed, leaving just the first and last letters
trashed means wrecked, so the letters of the word are scrambled

explanation.surface: A deserted secondary modern school is vandalised.
explanation.walkthrough: A secondary modern is a British state school type; here 'empty' leaves SY and 'is trashed' scrambles MODERN into NDROME.
explanation.definitionFit: A medical condition's set of symptoms, taken together, are the signs of a disorder.
